nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfidation
nodes.procedure: Typically, a piece of NF (1 cm × 3 cm) was immersed into a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave containing 10 mL of aqueous thiourea solution (1.445 mmol/L). The autoclave was then sealed and kept at 150 °C for 5 h. The material was taken out and washed with ethanol three times and dried in vacuum at room temperature, giving the Ni3S2/NF material as product.

nodes.name: Partial cation exchange
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, a piece of Ni3S2/NF was immersed into a mixture solution containing cobaltous acetate tetrahydrate (0.622 g) and ethylene glycol (30 mL) in a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave. The autoclave was then sealed and maintained at 200 °C for 12 h. The resulting material was washed with water and ethanol several times and dried at room temperature, giving the NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF material.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals three-dimensional macroporous foam-like structure with vertically oriented nanosheets of ca. 20 nm thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF (Fig. 2A and B) reveal that the material has a three-dimensional macroporous foam-like structure, and its surface is covered uniformly with a mass of vertically oriented nanosheets with a thickness of ca. 20 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms vertically grown nanosheets maintaining morphology of underlying Ni3S2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of vertically grown nanosheets is further supported by transmission electron microscopy (TEM, Fig. 2C).

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing nanostructured material with circular features and lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows monodispersed nanoparticles 3-5 nm on nanosheets with lattice fringes of 0.235 nm corresponding to (400) planes of cubic NixCo3-xS4 phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A closer observation of the nanosheets of NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF by high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) reveals that the nanosheets contain a lot of monodispersed nanoparticles with 3-5 nm in size on them (Fig. 2D). Additional HRTEM images (Figs. 2E and 2F) further reveal that these nanoparticles have two sets of lattice fringes with the same interplanar spacing of 0.235 nm corresponding to the (400) crystallographic planes of cubic NixCo3-xS4 phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern reveals diffraction rings characteristic of NixCo3-xS4 nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 2G) reveals a set of diffraction rings that are characteristic of NixCo3-xS4 nanocrystals, confirming the presence of such nanocrystals on the nanosheets of NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows homogeneous nanoscale distribution of Ni, Co, and S over entire nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping of the material (Fig. S2 in SI) shows that all the elements that are expected to be present in the material, i.e., Ni, Co and S, are there and are homogeneously distributed at nanoscale over the entire nanosheets of the material.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows weak bands below 450 cm⁻¹ attributed to Ni3S2 and bands above 450 cm⁻¹ ascribed to NixCo3-xS4, confirming presence of both phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectrum of NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF, a set of weak Raman bands in wavenumber region below 450 cm⁻¹ that can be attributed to Ni3S2 and a set of Raman bands in the wavenumber region above 450 cm⁻¹ that can be ascribed to NixCo3-xS4 are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows crystalline Ni3S2 and metallic nickel; NixCo3-xS4 peaks not observable due to ultrasmall size and low density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF (Fig. S4 in SI) shows that the material contains crystalline Ni3S2 and metallic nickel.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS suggests no strong electronic interaction between NixCo3-xS4 and Ni3S2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: results obtained by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, Fig. S3 in SI) suggest that there is no strong electronic interaction between NixCo3-xS4 and Ni3S2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show charge transfer resistance Rct values of 26.1 Ω for NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF, 83.7 Ω for Ni3S2/NF, and 32.7 Ω for NixCo3-xS4/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on their fitting equivalent circuit model, the values of charge transfer resistance in these three materials are found to be 83.7, 32.7 and 26.1 Ω, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates used to determine double-layer capacitance Cdl; ECSA values are 350.5 cm² for NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF, 187.5 cm² for Ni3S2/NF, and 192.5 cm² for NixCo3-xS4/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Plots of the difference in current density (J) between the anodic and cathodic sweeps (J_anodic – J_cathodic) at 0.15 V vs. RHE against the scan rate is plotted. The slope of the fitted line on the data points is then used to determine the double-layer capacitance (Cdl), and finally to estimate the electrochemical surface area (ECSA)... The effective electrode surface areas of Ni3S2/NF, NixCo3-xS4/NF and NixCo3-xS4/Ni3S2/NF are found to be 187.5, 192.5 and 350.5 cm², respectively.
